texts: The spinning wheel of the wicked turns out only tangled yarns of deceit; sweet is the peace of the one who keeps away.
Write a doha about how a spiteful man, like a spinning wheel that endlessly spins out stories and plots, wears down everyone near him, and the wise answer is not to quarrel but to quietly step aside.
A neighbour of ours sits at her spinning wheel all day spinning rumours about everyone on the lane, and she smiles at us each evening; I want a doha about handling a person like that.
spinning wheel, wicked person
hey doha pls on cruel people: they spin the spinning wheel of lies all day and you get tangled, so how to stay clear
My landlord promises everything with a warm smile, then breaks every promise like a dry leaf crumbling in his hand, and I'd like a doha on dealing with such a man.
wicked man, leaf
doha pls: a wicked man's promises are like dry leaves, they blow off at the first wind, so don't count on them

Compose a doha explaining that the vile will say sweet words but their promises fall like autumn leaves, so the sensible person neither trusts them nor fights them, but simply walks his path with care.
A crumpled leaf is the word of the wicked, torn by the lightest breath; trust it not, nor wrestle with it.
My boss enjoys humiliating people in meetings, and nothing we say changes him; how do you live near someone who is like this? Maybe a doha will tell me.
wicked people, stay away
Please craft a couplet for me about the cruel and cunning man who hurts others for his pleasure, saying that arguing with him is useless and that the wise protect themselves by distance and silence.
The wicked take joy in another's grief; leave them to their own sorrow and walk on in peace.
doha pls on how to deal with nasty people at work
bridge, wicked man
The wicked cross the bridge on others' backs and break it when they reach the other bank; guard your bridge, O traveller of the world.
doha: wicked people burn the bridge after they cross it, so don't let them cross yours
There's a man in our village who crosses every bridge by pushing others aside, and then burns the bridge behind him; I need a doha on how to deal with someone like that.
Write a doha saying that a wicked man uses people like a bridge, crossing over them to reach his gain, and once he has crossed he forgets them and even destroys the way back, so keep your distance.
The river flows toward all, yet the wicked drink and then foul it; walk upstream, away from such company.
The factory owner by our river has polluted it without a care, and when villagers asked, he laughed in our faces; a doha on dealing with someone so selfish, please.

Compose a doha that tells how the river does not turn back to purify itself, and the malicious man is likewise past advice, so the wise draw their water elsewhere and leave him to his own muddy current.
yo doha idea: a wicked person is like dirty river water, you can't clean it by arguing
river, wicked, stay clear
false scales, leaf, cheat
The scales of the evil are crooked and their leaf of promise is thin; no honest soul can trade with them.
Make me a doha saying that the ruthless man uses false scales, giving less and taking more, and his words are as flimsy as a leaf in the wind, so one should not deal with him or expect justice.
A shopkeeper in our area shows a falling leaf of paper as his licence and cheats customers with false scales; I'd like a doha about dealing with such cheats.
doha pls: the wicked weigh everything on crooked scales, and they only seem to fall like leaves when caught
Two faces has the cruel: one that smiles upon you, one that plots behind your back; keep your distance from both.
doha about people who act sweet but stab you in the back
deceitful smiler
I tried to be kind to a coworker who smiles at me, then spreads lies behind my back; I don't know how to deal with someone like that. Could you write a doha?
Write a doha on the cruel person who flatters us in public and slanders us in private, saying that one need not fight him, but must never open one's heart to his sweet words.
gold, furnace, wicked
Put raw ore in the furnace and it shines; put the cruel in the same heat and they only harden: such is their unchanging stubbornness.
Write a doha saying that gold becomes purer in the furnace but the cruel heart only gets harder by every attempt to heat it with advice, so the wise leave the vile alone to their own ways.
I've tried for years to reform my cousin, who cheats everyone, but he is as hard as before; I think the furnace of life hasn't changed him at all. Can you write a doha?
doha pls: you can melt gold in a furnace, but you can't melt a wicked heart, don't waste your time
moth, sandalwood, jealous
The moth gnaws at sandalwood but cannot spoil its scent; so the noble stay calm before the spite of the wicked.

Can you make a doha that says the malicious are moths who attack the good out of envy, yet sandalwood stays fragrant even when it is eaten, teaching the noble to remain calm and not to answer spite with spite.
doha pls: wicked people are like moths who ruin every sandalwood chest they get into, quietly eating it from inside

A neighbour's jealousy was like a moth that kept eating the sandalwood chest his grandfather had left to us, and finally he got what he wanted; make a doha about dealing with a jealous person like that.
I lent money to a man who has hurt many, thinking it would change him; instead he now mocks me, and I realise how silly I was. Could you write a doha?
Beware the wicked, they are not made kind by kindness nor tamed by gifts; step away in silence.
yo doha on why being nice to evil people doesn't work
avoid the evil
I want a doha that explains that giving a favour to a wicked person only makes him bolder, because he takes kindness for weakness, and so the wise are courteous but never get too close.
Strive not with the wicked, for quarrel is what they crave; withdraw in silence and leave them with nothing.
doha idea: dont argue with cruel people, they enjoy the fight
I used to try to win over my mean uncle with gifts and compliments, but he only grew more demanding; now I just keep my distance. Please write a doha of this lesson.
Write a doha saying that the best response to an evil person is neither anger nor flattery but quiet distance, because he feeds on reaction and weakens when nobody gives him any.
keep distance, wicked
The local landlord gave out cloth sheets to beggars on the festival and made sure the cameras were there, but he evicted three families the same week; I want a doha about it.
cloth sheet, beggar, false giver
The cloth sheet the wicked hand to the beggar is a bait; there is a price on every gift the false one gives.
Compose a doha that says the ruthless sometimes give a small gift to a beggar or a poor man only to show off, and a wise person should not be fooled by such generosity but see the greed behind it.
doha pls: a wicked rich man gives a cloth sheet to a beggar for a photo, then takes ten times back, don't be fooled by their charity
doha plz about how to spot fake nice people
Pen a doha that tells us that the cruel person is known not by his words but by his deeds, and so we must watch what he does with the weak and powerless before trusting him with anything.
The cunning smile is false and the soft word is a trap; look not at what the wicked say but at what they do.
beware the cunning
A colleague of mine always compliments me to my face but takes credit for my work; how should one deal with such a person? Maybe a doha can tell me.

Write a doha saying that the speech of the vile looks like milk, pure and white, but hides an arrow that pierces the trusting, and the wise person listens carefully for the sharpness behind sweetness.
doha pls: a wicked man's talk is milk outside, arrow inside, beware
Sweet as milk are the words of the wicked, yet the arrow lies hidden in the cup; sip, and the wound is sure.
My grandfather said the cruel man's words are sweet like milk but carry an arrow, and I saw this when my cousin trusted a salesman who sold him a fraud; write a doha about it.
milk, arrow, wicked talk
Compose a doha that tells us not to judge a man by his visits to the temple or his show of devotion, because a wicked man can hide his nature behind piety until it is too late.
A trader in our town visits the temple every morning with a big tilak but cheats widows over the counter; please write a doha about his kind.
doha pls: some wicked people go to the temple every day but their hearts are the same, don't be fooled by looks
temple, hypocrite
The hypocrites bow at the temple steps and carry daggers in their hearts; devotion rings false.
I begged my cruel landlord for a few more days to pay the rent, and he looked at me as if I were a piece of stone; maybe a doha will help me forget him.
Pour sweet words upon a stone and it remains a stone; so too the wicked cannot be moved by kindness or by sermons.
stone-hearted, wicked
doha pls: some people are like stone, nothing you say moves them, just leave them
I want a doha saying that the malicious person has a heart of stone, on which neither kindness, nor tears, nor wise sayings can leave an impression, so the wise do not waste their breath on him.
yo doha on dealing with a toxic person without fighting
I'd like a doha that tells the gentle to protect themselves from malicious people with firmness, not hatred, because hating them tires the soul, but distance keeps it peaceful.
After my ex hurt me for years, I realised I did not have to hate him, I only had to stop seeing him, and now I breathe easier; I want a doha for this.
Love the wicked from afar; hate them not, near them not; let the heart keep its calm.
evil people, stay safe
A man in our town grinds the poor with high interest, working them like a grindstone works grain, and no complaint stops him; write a doha about him.
Compose a doha that says the evil person uses others like a grindstone uses grain, crushing them for his gain without feeling, and that the wise should not feed him with their time, trust, or labour.
doha pls: a cruel man grinds the weak like a grindstone, stay away from his mill
The wicked turn the grindstone against the poor, and the grain of their hopes is ground to dust.
grindstone, wicked, cruel
doha on how some people look holy like a heron but hunt in secret, how to deal with them

Write a doha saying that the ruthless man puts on the calm of a heron, standing still and saintly, while he watches for his chance to catch the unwary, and the wise do not mistake his stillness for innocence.
My neighbour speaks in whispers about duty and fasting, but he cheated his own brother out of land; I want a doha about such pious villains and what to do with them.
heron, hypocrite
The heron stands in silent prayer, yet his thoughts are on his prey; so the wicked wear holiness as a cloak.
The bully at my son's school never gets punished because his father is powerful; my son asked how to deal with him, so I need a doha with some advice.
bully, avoid
Mighty is the cruel, yet weak is his friendship; walk away with calm and let him face his own end.
I'd like a doha on the cruel person who uses power to frighten others, saying that the wise do not meet his anger with anger but protect themselves with patience and the courage to leave him behind.
doha idea about how to handle a bully without becoming one
I trusted a stranger who offered to guide me through an unfamiliar city, and he led me to his friends who took my wallet; make a doha about it, as a traveler.
traveler, false guide
Write a doha that says a traveler on the road of life must be careful of those who offer help too eagerly, since the wicked often wear the face of a friend to lead the unwary into their traps.
doha pls: some people are like fake guides, they lead the traveler to the robber's place, so check before you follow
The traveller who follows the smile of a stranger often finds himself at a robber's gate.
doha pls: even the philosopher's stone can't fix a wicked person, so don't try
I gave my cousin every chance, every support, as if I held a philosopher's stone that could change his life, but he turned each into a scheme to cheat; please write a doha.

Compose a doha explaining that even the philosopher's stone, which transforms every metal it touches, cannot change a wicked heart, who ruins every blessing received, so the wise keep their treasure and time away from such people.
Though the wicked held the philosopher's stone, he would turn its magic to dust; none can transform such a heart.
philosopher's stone, wicked touch
refuse the malicious
When the wicked invite you to share their scheme, refuse; the price of that bargain is your honour.
doha pls on how not to get dragged into other people's evil schemes
My colleagues planned to cheat the company and asked me to join, saying everyone does it; I said no and now they ignore me, and I'd like a doha for the courage to stay clean.
Give me a doha saying that the evil will invite you to share in their schemes by saying everybody does it, and the strong person says no, bearing their anger rather than a lifelong shame.
My neighbour, who cheats half the town, jumps at every knock on his gate; I realised cruelty doesn't let a person sleep. Could you write a doha?
wicked, fear not
doha pls: wicked people look powerful but they're really scared inside

Write a doha that says the ruthless, though they seem strong, live in constant fear of being found out and punished, and so the honest person need not tremble but only go his way with a clear conscience.
The cruel sleep without peace, and their riches bring no rest; fear them not, but pity them.
doha about jealous people, you can't please them
envious ones, ignore

Compose a doha saying that the envious person cannot be satisfied by any amount of kindness, because his happiness depends on your failure, so the wise stop seeking his approval and simply live their days.
There is a man in my office who laughs when others fail and sulks when others succeed, and nothing improves him; I would love a doha about people like this and how to deal with them.
The envious weep at your joy and laugh at your fall; give them no audience, and let envy consume itself.
Better to walk alone than as a traveler beside the cruel; the road is long and the guide is untrue.
On my trip I travelled with some rough strangers who looked friendly, but they stole from me in the night; I would love a doha to remind other travelers to avoid such company.

Please craft a couplet for the traveler on life's path, teaching that one should rather walk alone than keep company with those who use deceit, since the road of the vile ends in the pit they dug for others.
traveler, wicked company
doha pls: if the road is full of robbers it's better to wait than to travel with the wicked
wicked fall in time
doha pls: wicked people always get caught eventually, so be patient
Cruelty is a poor ruler; the wicked prosper a season and are forgotten; the patient outlive them.
Write a doha that comforts those who suffer under the malicious, saying that their power is temporary and their deeds follow them, so the wise bear it with patience and let time do its justice.
My old boss who bullied everybody was fired last month, and the whole department quietly smiled; it made me believe that bad people fall in the end. Could you write a doha?
wicked, deal with silence
Answer the cruel with silence, and their words return upon themselves; peace is the only victory.
doha idea: the best answer to a fool is silence
Compose a doha that teaches that the wise do not waste words on the wicked, because every argument gives them more to twist, and silence leaves them with nothing to attack and nothing to win.
I stopped replying to my cousin's insulting messages three months ago, and the insults have dried up by themselves; I'd like a doha out of that experience.
heron, elephant, wicked
The heron's stillness hides a hunger, the elephant's strength hides a rage; beware the wicked who wear both.

Make me a doha that warns the wise about the ruthless who show quiet cunning like the heron and brute force like the elephant, and who destroy others without caring, so one should stay far from their path.
doha plz: wicked folks can be calm like a heron then trample like an elephant, don't be fooled
A man in our area looks as quiet as a heron and as strong as an elephant, yet he uses both for plotting and trampling; write a doha on how to deal with such wicked men.
The false pearl gleams like the true, but one touch shows the glass; so, too, the wicked, dressed in virtue.
Write a doha saying that the cruel often resemble a fake pearl, shining like truth while having no depth, and only a wise eye and a little patience will expose their true worth before it is too late.
doha pls: a wicked man is like a pearl made of glass, shiny outside but fake, so don't trust shiny people
false pearl, wicked
I bought a pearl necklace from a smooth-talking seller who swore it was genuine, but it was glass, and he laughed when I came back; please write a doha about people like that.
A distant relative shoots spiteful remarks at me every wedding, and I've decided to stop attending his events; please write a doha about the arrows of such people.
The cruel word is a silent arrow that wounds from afar; bless the one who walks beyond its range.
doha pls: some people shoot arrows with their words, best to stay out of range
Compose a doha about the cruel person whose words are like arrows, shot to hurt and not to heal, saying that the wise withdraw from his range rather than try to catch every arrow.
arrow, cruel words
deal with wicked, calmly

Can you make a doha saying that the wise person should not take revenge on the malicious or sink to their level, because calm and honest living is the strongest answer and the best way to expose their lies.
When my neighbour tried to spread rumours about my family, we ignored him and carried on; now no one believes him anymore, and I'd love a doha out of this.
doha idea: don't take revenge on the wicked, just move on, it hurts them more
Meet not malice with wrath; let calm be your strength, and their schemes will fail of themselves.
musk deer, hunted goodness

Compose a doha explaining that the evil often target the good precisely because they carry a fragrance of honesty that the ruthless cannot stand, and that the virtuous must remain wise, alert, and unbowed.
doha pls: a musk deer's fragrance gets it hunted, and the good get targeted by wicked people just for being good
The musk deer is hunted for its fragrance; so the virtuous are hunted by the wicked for their goodness.
My honest colleague gets bullied for refusing to join the others' schemes, like a musk deer hunted for its scent, and I'd like a doha for him.
The greedy are never full; whatever you give, their hands remain open and their wants remain endless.
wicked, endless greed
doha pls about greedy people who never get enough, how to deal with them
I kept giving my cousin money whenever he asked, and each time he asked for more with a new excuse; I finally stopped, and I would like a doha on this lesson.
Write a doha saying that the cruel and greedy can never be satisfied by any amount of wealth or favour, and so the wise stop feeding their hunger and use their means for the honest and the needy.
Beware, O traveller, the cup of milk offered by a stranger; the wicked sweeten their snare with kindness.
doha pls: a traveler shouldn't accept milk from a stranger, wicked people drug it, stay alert
The salesman on the train offered milk and food to the traveler next to me, and the poor man woke up robbed; I want a doha about wicked folk who disguise themselves as kind strangers.
Pen a doha for the traveler warning that the vile often come offering milk and food with a smile, and the careful man accepts nothing from a stranger whose purpose he does not know.
milk, traveler, trap
The touchstone tests the metal; the yogi tests the heart; blessed is the one who sees the wicked behind a smile.
touchstone, yogi, wicked
Our village yogi has an eye that, like a touchstone, sees through the fake and the cheat in a single glance, and the cheats fear him; please write a doha about this.

Write a doha that says a yogi's wisdom works like a touchstone, telling the pure from the false in a moment, and the wise person trains his eye to see the nature of the malicious before he lets them close.
doha pls: the touchstone shows what is real and a yogi can see real from fake in people, so be like that and avoid wicked folks
The seed of malice grows even in the shadow of kindness; the wicked can bear no good thing near them.
The seed of rivalry my cousin planted in our family has grown into a shadow over all of us; I would love a doha about how to avoid such wicked people.
Compose a doha showing that the evil person's seed of malice sprouts quickly and casts a dark shadow over all who stand near, so the wise plant themselves far from that shadow.
doha pls: the seed of hate grows a dark shadow of pain, avoid the ruthless person's shadow
seed, shadow, malice
doha plz: a pot of water seems full but a wicked person drains the pot when you're not looking
The chakor in me wanted to trust my business partner, but he kept draining the pot of water that was our shared savings, and I woke too late; write a doha about it.

I want a doha for those trusting by nature, like the chakor, saying that the cruel will take advantage of their faith and drain their resources like a cracked pot of water, so trust should be earned with time.
chakor, pot of water, wicked
The chakor gazes at the distant sky, trusting what it hopes for; the pot of water cracks, and the wicked take what was poured.

Compose a doha that says the malicious, like a tall date palm, are lofty but useless to the weary, giving neither shade nor fruit close at hand, and that a swan-like wise person should not expect help from them.
Tall as the date palm, yet it gives no shade to the swan; so the vile, though great, shelter no one.
swan, date palm, wicked
My cousin is rich and powerful like a tall date palm, and yet when the family needed him he did not even answer calls; I wish to write a doha about relying on wicked people.
doha pls: a swan sits under the date palm but the date palm gives no shade for the wicked, no help from them either
doha pls about fake yogis who rob the faithful, how to stay safe
The fake yogi in our neighbourhood hypnotised half the village and took their savings; I'd like a doha for those who trust false holy men and how to deal with him.
The wicked wear saffron as others wear armour; beneath it, the same hunger.
fake yogi, wicked
Write a doha that warns people that a false yogi can be the most dangerous of the evil, because he borrows holy words to hide his greed, so one must test a holy man by his deeds.
I'd like a doha showing that the ruthless person, like a moth drawn to a glare, is pulled by his own anger and malice into a self-made ruin, and that the wise only need to stay away.
I watched my cruel neighbour fall into debt and illness after years of tormenting others, like a moth drawn to its own ruin; please write a doha.
The moth circles the glare he cannot resist; the cruel circle spite till they burn in it.
doha pls: a moth dies chasing the glare because it can't stop, the wicked also destroy themselves by their own spite
moth, wicked spite
doha: wicked people are like the sun at noon, you can't look at them or get close, just stay in the shade
sun, cruel power
That boss of mine shines like the sun in front of the owners and burns everyone below him; I'd love a doha on how to handle such a person.
The wicked are as the noonday sun, scorching those below; keep away and walk in shade.
Write a doha which says the vile person in power is like the midday sun that scorches all who live near it, and the wise stay out of his path and under the cover of their own quiet work.
The wicked are like the leaf that floats on the stream, joining whichever way the water goes; no loyalty is theirs.
leaf, wicked, stay clear
Write a doha that says the malicious have no fixed loyalty and, like a leaf that is tossed here and there, side with whoever is powerful, and so the wise do not lean on them in hard times.
doha pls: wicked people follow whoever is winning, like leaves in the wind, never rely on them
A man I know changes his loyalty as often as a leaf changes direction in the breeze, and he betrayed us when we were weakest; I need a doha about such people.
sand, net, wicked
doha plz: wicked people build on sand and set nets for others, but their own fortunes sink
Give me a doha that says the evil cast nets for others but build their own fortune on the sand of lies, so they do not last long, and the wise only need to avoid their nets with patience.
The net of the wicked is spread on shifting sand, and the catch is only their own ruin.
A man in our town cast a net of false cases around his rivals and built his empire on sand, but it all collapsed last year; I want a doha.
The cleric wears white cotton, but the whiteness stops at the skin; keep away from the wicked who wear piety as a robe.
A cleric in our town wears the finest cotton robes, and speaks of piety, but cheats the orphans' fund; I'd like a doha on dealing with such men of religion.
cleric, cotton, hypocrite
Write a doha that says the ruthless sometimes hide behind spotless cotton robes and holy speeches of a cleric, and the wise judge a man by his deeds and not by how clean his garments are.
doha pls: a clean cotton robe doesn't make a clean cleric, some are wicked, be careful
After I stopped meeting my cruel relatives, my life became so calm that I wonder why I tolerated them for so long; could you write a doha?
Keep away from the wicked as you would from sickness; sweet are the days that pass without them.
avoid evil company
doha pls: wicked people should be avoided like a plague
Write a doha saying that the cruel bring trouble wherever they go, and a wise man arranges his life so that he sees them seldom, speaks to them briefly, and trusts them never.
washerman, wicked heart
doha pls: a washerman can wash dirty garments but not a dirty heart, evil people stay dirty
The washerman in our street can clean any stain but he said even he can't clean my cruel uncle's reputation; please write a doha about the wicked.
Please craft a couplet that says the washerman may remove the dirt from a person's garments but cannot clean the dirt of malice from a heart, so a wise man avoids those whose stains are inward.
The washerman cleanses the garment at the water's edge, yet no washing can cleanse an evil mind.
wicked, calm response
The cruel mock the humble now, but time will mock them in return; be calm and keep your path.
doha pls: how to keep your cool around mean people
Write a doha that teaches patience in the face of the vile, saying that the humble should not be provoked into anger by their taunts, because anger is the reward that the malicious seek.
My neighbours made fun of our small dwelling for years, and I never answered back; now they come to us asking for help, and I want a doha about this.
Leave the cruel behind, and the heart grows lighter, the day grows kinder, and peace returns.

Compose a doha that says the greatest freedom comes from walking away from the ruthless, those who drain our patience, steal our peace and give nothing back, and that this distance is no cruelty but wisdom.
doha pls: leaving wicked people is the best gift you give yourself
leave wicked ones
I finally walked away from a friend who had lied and cheated for years, and my life became lighter; a doha for those who stay too long with the wicked, please.
Make me a doha that says the vile bark at the noble like dogs at the moon, and like a drop of sour in milk they spoil what is pure, so the noble walk on in calm and keep distance.
The moon-like calm of my teacher never broke even when a wicked rival tried to spoil his name like a drop of sour on milk; please write a doha about him.
The moon keeps her cool light though the cur may howl; the cruel bark, the noble walk on.
doha pls: the moon stays cool in the sky even though dogs bark at it, and milk is spoiled by one drop of the wicked, ignore them
moon, milk, wicked
